f1.quote: The modulation period (individual layer thickness, λ) was varied among 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm by RF magnetron sputtering

f2.quote: Room-temperature nanoindentation used a 5 mN maximum load, loading rates of 1, 0.1, and 0.01 mN/s

f3.quote: a 100 s hold, and 20 s unloading; indentation depths were maintained at approximately 1/10–1/7 of the coating thickness

f4.quote: Deposition used a base pressure of about 5 × 10^-4 Pa, Ar flow of 100 sccm, working pressure of 0.3 Pa, 150 W on the HEA target, alternating 0/30 W on the Al target, and a 1 h deposition

f5.quote: M16 contained semicoherent FCC/BCC interfaces with misfit dislocations; M8 had coherent interfaces with continuous atomic planes

f6.quote: M32/M80 were dominated by grain boundaries because λ exceeded the approximately 20 nm grain diameter

f7.quote: Semicoherent interfaces strongly block dislocation glide, causing dislocation pileup and localized high stress

f8.quote: Stress-induced interfacial amorphization in M16 is invoked based partly on the authors' prior MD/HRTEM work rather than directly established here.

f9.quote: Relative to multilayers dominated by coherent interfaces or grain boundaries, the λ = 16 nm semicoherent multilayer exhibits the greatest room-temperature creep resistance

f11.quote: coherent-interface- or grain-boundary-dominated samples therefore deform mainly by dislocation slip or climb
